entities.name: Vahriz
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Vahriz, also known as Wahrez, was a highly accomplished Sasanian general of Daylamite origin, whose military prowess under Khosrow I Anushirvan (r. 531–579 CE) fundamentally reshaped the geopolitical landscape of the Arabian Peninsula in the late 6th century CE. His campaigns marked a pivotal moment in the Sasanian Empire's expansionist ambitions, extending Persian influence into regions previously dominated by the Aksumite Kingdom and laying groundwork for the complex power dynamics of pre-Islamic Arabia. Vahriz's actions decisively established a Sasanian client state in Yemen, a strategic move that significantly impacted trade routes and regional control.

His military career is first noted in the prelude to the Iberian War (526–532 CE), though his most celebrated achievements occurred during the Aksumite–Persian wars. Around 570 CE, responding to appeals from the Himyarite prince Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan for assistance against Aksumite rule, Vahriz led a modest but highly effective Sasanian expeditionary force, reportedly numbering 800 men, to Yemen. Utilizing a fleet of eight ships, he landed near Aden, where his troops, equipped with superior Sasanian military technology, including advanced archery and tactical discipline, decisively defeated the Aksumite viceroy Masruq ibn Abraha. This swift victory led to the re-establishment of Himyarite rule under Sasanian suzerainty, effectively ending Aksumite dominance in the region and incorporating Yemen into the Sasanian sphere of influence.
